forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329074016_d9949d95
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

payload.statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate and define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when a = b. For each nonnegative integer n, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j), with (q;q)_0 := 1. Then one has the identity in the rational function field Z(q): P_{a,b,r}(q) = ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b).

result_payload.proof_nl:
Because 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, the integers a, b, r+a, and r+b are all nonnegative, so every q-Pochhammer symbol appearing in the claimed identity is defined.

First consider the case a = b. By the definition of P_{a,b,r}(q), the product from i = a+1 to b is empty, so P_{a,b,r}(q) = 1. On the other hand,
((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b)
= ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_a)
= 1.
So the identity holds when a = b.

Now assume a < b. We use the following elementary consequence of the definition of (q;q)_n: for any nonnegative integers m < n,
(q;q)_n = (q;q)_m \prod_{j=m+1}^n (1 - q^j).
Indeed, if m = 0 then this is just (q;q)_n = 1 \cdot \prod_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j), using (q;q)_0 = 1; if m > 0, it follows by splitting the defining product for (q;q)_n after the factor j = m.

Apply this with m = r+a and n = r+b. Since a < b, we have r+a < r+b, so
(q;q)_{r+b} = (q;q)_{r+a} \prod_{j=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^j).
Apply it again with m = a and n = b:
(q;q)_b = (q;q)_a \prod_{j=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^j).

Since each factor 1 - q^j is a nonzero polynomial, these products are invertible in the rational function field Z(q). Therefore,
((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b)
= \frac{\prod_{j=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^j)}{\prod_{j=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^j)}.

Now reindex the numerator by writing j = r+i. As j runs from r+a+1 to r+b, the index i runs from a+1 to b. Hence
\prod_{j=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^j) = \prod_{i=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^{r+i}).
Substituting this gives
((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b)
= \frac{\prod_{i=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^{r+i})}{\prod_{i=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^i)}
= \prod_{i=a+1}^{b} \frac{1 - q^{r+i}}{1 - q^i}
= P_{a,b,r}(q),
where the last equality is exactly the definition of P_{a,b,r}(q).

Thus, in all cases,
P_{a,b,r}(q) = ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b)
in the rational function field Z(q).
result_payload.proof_summary: Handle a=b separately. For a<b, expand q-Pochhammer symbols using (q;q)_n = (q;q)_m \prod_{j=m+1}^n (1-q^j), apply this to (m,n)=(r+a,r+b) and (a,b), cancel the common initial factors in Z(q), then reindex j=r+i.
